study_id: Mardini et al. - 2024 - An explainable machine learning approach using contemporary UNOS data to identify patients who fail

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant candidates using a non‑linear machine learning model (XGBoost) to predict waitlist failure, includes relevant outcomes and is a peer‑reviewed article published after 2018.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: National Institutes of Health (NIH) via UL1TR001427 award
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of UNOS registry data to develop and validate an explainable ML model predicting failure of status 2 bridge to heart transplantation.
identification_methods.Institution: University of Florida, Department of Health Outcomes and Biomedical Informatics, Gainesville, FL, United States
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult heart transplant candidates listed as UNOS Status 2 and supported with Impella (5.0 or 5.5) or intra‑aortic balloon pump between 2018 and 2022.
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Addressed using SMOTE, under‑sampling and class weighting; best approach selected per model.
identification_methods.Input Variables: 19 UNOS variables including demographics, BMI, height, race, smoking history, blood group, device type, implanted defibrillator, mechanical ventilation, dialysis, multiorgan transplant, hemodynamics (PAPi, etc.), biochemistry (creatinine, sodium, etc.), medications and UNOS region.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Evaluated mean, median, K‑nearest neighbor, and XGBoost built‑in imputation; selected optimal method per model.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Hyperparameter tuning via grid search; model interpretation using SHAP values; internal validation with nested CV; performance metrics reported include AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity.

population.Inclusion criteria: Heart transplant candidates listed as UNOS Status 2 between 2018 and 2022 and supported with Impella (5.0 or 5.5) or intra-aortic balloon pump
population.Exclusion criteria: UNOS region 6 excluded due to <150 patients
population.Target Population: Patients listed as Status 2 awaiting heart transplantation (bridge to transplant)
population.Population Notes: Cohort includes all UNOS regions except region 6; data derived from contemporary UNOS registry (2018‑2022)

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: UNOS registry clinical variables (demographic, hemodynamic, biochemical, device and treatment features)
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: Variables selected based on statistical significance and removal of highly correlated features
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data at time of listing
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: XGBoost models built with nested 5×5 cross‑validation, grid search hyperparameter tuning, evaluation of multiple imputation and class‑imbalance strategies
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Primary outcome: failure of UNOS Status 2 listing (death, too sick, inactive status 7 or upgrade to status 1); model performance metrics AUC, accuracy, balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Failure defined as death while on waitlist, being too sick for transplant, inactive status 7 or upgrade to status 1
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Comprehensive model AUC 0.71 ± 0.03 (range across regions 0.44–0.74), specificity 0.75–0.96, accuracy 0.69–0.90
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All UNOS Status 2 heart transplant candidates supported with IABP or Impella (n=4,178)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUC calculated on independent test folds of a 5×5 nested cross‑validation
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Model shows high specificity but limited sensitivity for predicting failure during Status 2 period
